overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the executive session stayed within the noticed complaint topic, the open-session social media announcement was not reasonably anticipated, and the free speech claim was declined as outside the OML.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the committee discussed a topic at its June 19 meeting that was not on the posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: After reviewing the Committee’s June 19 executive session minutes, in camera, we are satisfied that the discussion remained within the noticed topic.

allegations.summary: The chair's open-session announcement about social media use and the liaison role was allegedly not listed on the meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: it was not required to be included on the meeting notice

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged that having a single social media spokesperson violates the federal constitutional right to free speech.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.
